newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX Hub natgas still down late, Mar cash holds.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX Hub natgas still down late, Mar cash holds.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures remained mostly lower late Monday in thin activity, with April still flirting with near-support despite talk of relatively steady March cash prices, industry sources said.
At 1400 EST, April was still down by 1.1 cents at $1.81 per million British thermal units. May remained two cents lower at $1.855, while others were down by 0.3 to two cents.

"The momentum feels like it is starting to switch from the sell side to the buy side. We're starting to lose some of the spec sellers," said one East Coast trader, noting forward paper basis differentials were up from recent lows.

He noted April-October quotes for gas in New York were in the NYMEX plus 24 to plus 26 cent range, up from 23 cents over done last week. Some Gulf Coast and Appalachian differentials also saw similar gains, he said.
"NYMEX looks like there's support in the $1.70s (basis April), but I'm afraid if we get another bearish storage number (Wednesday), it may not hold," the East Coast trader said.

With few extremes in temperatures predicted for this week, many expected March physical prices to crater once flows began. And while milder midweek forecasts and ample eastern storage were likely to keep the market on the defensive near-term, opinions about market direction did seem more mixed this week, traders said.

"We've met some of the technical objectives and the stochs (stochastics) say we're oversold, so you could believe we're at or near the bottom," said one eastern utility source. But he said trending markets can remain overbought or oversold for quite a while before reversing.

Technically, traders said an April close below support at $1.80 could lead to a move to the mid-$1.70s and possibly a test of the contract low of $1.701. Resistance was still seen at $1.93 and then at $2.04.

In the physical market, Gulf Coast gas was little changed Monday in the mid-to-high $1.70s. Most Midcon pipes were talked steady in the mid-$1.60s. New York city gate swing gas was unchanged to five cents higher in the $2.15 area.
NYMEX said 14,104 Hub contracts traded as of 1315 EST. Hub open interest on Feb 28 rose 2,003 contracts to 160,180.
NYMEX Alberta and Permian natgas were untraded at 1345 EST.
On the KCBT, April was still down by five cents at $1.58, while deferreds remained two to three cents lower. The East/West spread widened by 3.9 cents to 23.0 cents (NYMEX premium).
